verses.1: The words of Agoor ben-Yakheh, who proclaimed that the kingdom belongs to Elijah, forever and ever.
verses.2: For I am like a man who is separated from others, and no one understands me.
verses.3: And I did not learn wisdom or knowledge of the sacred matters. I do not know them at all.
verses.4: Who raised the heavens? Who descended from above? Who filled their garments with air? Who created all the creatures of the earth? What is their name, and what are their deeds?
verses.5: Every word of God is a shield for protection.
verses.6: Do not add anything to his words, otherwise they will not be true for you, and you will be deceived.
verses.7: I asked you twice from you: do not avoid me before I can hear the truth.
verses.8: Let those false words be far away from me. Do not give me any food that is unclean.
verses.9: I will not be deceived, nor will I say anything false. I will speak only what Jehovah says. And I will not steal or take anything from my God’s place.
verses.10: Do not speak to your master in a way that might cause him to be angry with you.
verses.11: His father will scold him, and he will not bless his mother.
verses.12: He lived in a world of evil, and he never wanted to leave it.
verses.13: Let his eyes and eyelids be removed from their place.
verses.14: The food that comes from destroyed cities and the scraps of food left over from their destruction can be eaten by the poor from the land, and by the elderly who have no one to provide them with food.
verses.15: For the two daughters of the householder, who are now old and no longer able to work, they will not be rewarded. They were not worthy of being praised at all.
verses.16: Shaul and Ezer, who are merciful to the earth; they do not measure it with waters. And fire, which never speaks.
verses.17: Let them mock their father and despise their mother. May they be destroyed by the evening wind, and may the sons of Nacher eat them.
verses.18: Three of them fell from me, and four others were unknown to me.
verses.19: The path that is taken in the heavens, the path that is like a snake’s body, the path that goes through the heart of the sea, and the path that goes through the sky.
verses.20: And so, through a woman who was in a state of distress, she ate and chewed her food, and said, “I didn’t do anything.”
verses.21: Under six years, the earth will be angry; and under four years, it will not be able to stand.
verses.22: Under the rule of a tyrant, he will reign; but when he is overthrown, he will be destroyed.
verses.23: Under the curse, for when you marry and have children, you will inherit your wife’s property.
verses.24: They are four of them; they are little people. And they are all wise and intelligent people.
verses.25: The swallows did not dare to approach, and they prepared themselves for battle.
verses.26: They were with those who were not righteous, and they placed them in the house of their own homes.
verses.27: The king of Ein Larba went out and built a wall with all his strength.
verses.28: It is in hands that it should be held, and it lies within the palace of the king.
verses.29: Three are suitable for walking, and four are suitable for climbing.
verses.30: He will reign over the animals, and he will not return from all of this.
verses.31: Zarzir Matanayim or Taish, and King Alkum with him.
verses.32: If you are in a state of despair, and if your hands are trembling.
verses.33: For milk juice produces heat, while nosebleeds and bleeding from the gums cause inflammation.
